summary: config.py holds the AWS documentation example key pair as literals. The pair is rated critical, as the checklist requires. No other hard-coded secrets turned up in the five files in the repository.

findings.title: AWS example access key ID hard-coded
findings.evidence: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "AKIA..." (the AWS documentation example key ID, ending in EXAMPLE)
findings.recommendation: Remove the literal and read the key from the environment or a secret store, or use an IAM role. Rotate it if it was ever real.

findings.title: AWS example secret access key hard-coded
findings.recommendation: Remove the literal and load the secret from the environment or a secret store. Rotate it if it was ever real.

limitations: The repository has only five files, and I read all of them. This step covers secrets only, so the debug mode, wildcard CORS and verify=False in app.py are not reported here.
